comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C3 and C37 regarding expression level importance over immunogenicity. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to limited evidence from single peptide comparison, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and explicitly highlight this as a key strength of the study.

Strong overlap on NAP-CNB platform capabilities (C1, C8-C10, C40-C43). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes performance metrics (C11-C12) which peer review addresses but OpenEval separately evaluates as UNCERTAIN in R2. Peer reviewers find platform capabilities 'convincing' without critique.

OpenEval rates performance metrics claims C11-C12 as UNCERTAIN due to lack of underlying benchmarking data. Peer review R1 includes these claims in their SUPPORTED evaluation of platform capabilities, accepting them without questioning the validation methodology.

High overlap on background context claims (C5-C7, C44-C49). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on citation accuracy and field representation, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the rationale as establishing an important research problem.

Both address multiantigen vaccination efficacy (C4, C38). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanism is inferred rather than demonstrated, while peer reviewers accept findings as contributing important information without questioning mechanistic details. Peer R5 also includes C30 which OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

Partial overlap on experimental design and immunogenicity validation. OpenEval R3 covers broader methodology (C13-C16, C52-C77) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R2 focuses on immunogenicity validation (C2, C13-C22) also rated SUPPORTED, with both finding the experimental approach convincing.

OpenEval R3 includes peptide selection methodology (C14-C16) as part of broader SUPPORTED methodology evaluation. Peer R6 specifically questions documentation of peptide selection rationale for these same claims, rating as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete manuscript documentation despite adequate author responses.

Substantial overlap on methodological claims (C52-C77). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of controls and standard practices. Peer reviewers implicitly accept methods as appropriate, with no concerns raised about experimental protocols or statistical approaches.

Both address immunogenicity assays (C17-C22). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate statistical analysis and adequate sample size for screening. Peer reviewers explicitly state authors 'proved in vivo that in silico-predicted neoantigens can trigger antitumor response.'

OpenEval R4 includes statistical methodology claims (C68-C69, C72) as part of immunogenicity validation rated SUPPORTED. Peer R8 includes these in broader methodological acceptance, with no concerns about statistical approaches.

Partial overlap on tumor challenge controls (C23-C26). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls and statistical methods for survival data. Peer R3 accepts these findings as demonstrating RNA expression importance, focusing on biological conclusions rather than methodological details.

OpenEval R5 includes tumor challenge methodology (C56, C58-C60, C71, C74) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R8 includes these claims in broader methodological acceptance without specific concerns about tumor challenge protocols.

Both address variable outcomes for individual peptides (C27-C29). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample sizes and lack of statistical significance. Peer R3 rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing the biological finding that RNA expression is important rather than questioning statistical power for individual peptides.

OpenEval R7 addresses multiantigen efficacy (C30, C34) rated SUPPORTED with caveat about small sample size. Peer R3 includes C34 and related claims in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of expression level importance, accepting the efficacy findings without sample size concerns.

Both address multiantigen vaccination effectiveness (C30, C34). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative outcomes and statistical significance while noting sample size limitations. Peer reviewers accept findings as contributing important information for neoantigen selection.

Both address Wiz peptide efficacy despite weaker immunogenicity (C31, C34). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this supports considering expression levels but cautions about small sample size. Peer reviewers highlight this as key evidence that RNA expression is very important for peptide selection.

Both address NAP-CNB validation (C2, C22, C35-C36). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes correlation between predictions and outcomes while noting generalizability limits. Peer reviewers accept validation as proving in silico predictions can trigger antitumor response.

Partial overlap on platform validation implications (C35-C36). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on predictive capability validation with caveats. Peer R7 addresses broader implications for personalized vaccination, finding evidence convincing and useful for clinical translation.

OpenEval R12 addresses quantitative effectiveness metrics (C32-C33) rated SUPPORTED with note about wide confidence intervals from small sample size. Peer R3 includes these claims in broader SUPPORTED evaluation without addressing statistical precision concerns.

OpenEval R13 addresses ICS methodology and bootstrap statistics (C70, C73) rated SUPPORTED but notes missing implementation details. Peer R8 includes these in broader methodological acceptance without concerns about statistical analysis documentation.

Both address Trp2 as positive control (C39). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates through citation and experimental performance. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of background context establishing study rationale.

Both address translational implications (C51). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting broad claims based on limited single-model validation. Peer R7 rates as SUPPORTED, accepting that findings contribute important information for personalized vaccination without questioning generalizability.

OpenEval R16 addresses translational claims (C50-C51) rated UNCERTAIN as speculative beyond demonstrated results. Peer R9 includes C50 in background context rated SUPPORTED, accepting the motivational framing without distinguishing demonstrated results from future potential.
